findings.title: gnn_type.py imports two GAT modules absent from the repo; every run crashes at import
findings.quote:
from triton_tests.gat import GATConv
from models.triton_nn.mean_gnn import TritonMeanGNN
from models.triton_nn.gat import TritonGAT
findings.claim: gnn_type.py unconditionally imports `triton_tests.gat.GATConv` and `models.triton_nn.gat.TritonGAT`, but no `gat.py` exists anywhere in the repo (only `triton_tests/test2d_mean.py`, `models/triton_nn/mean_gnn.py`, `models/triton_kernels/mean.py` are present).
findings.concern: Because main.py -> helpers.arguments -> helpers.gnn_type, `python main.py` raises ModuleNotFoundError at import for EVERY --gnn_type (MEAN_GNN and GAT), so no result in the paper can be reproduced; additionally TS-GAT (Table 1, Table 4) has no backbone implementation at all.
findings.resolution: Add the missing `triton_tests/gat.py` (GATConv) and `models/triton_nn/gat.py` (TritonGAT), or gate the GAT imports; confirm which commit produced the paper's numbers.

findings.title: DSS-Mean, TS-SGC, TS-GCN, TS-GCNII (Tables 5–6) are not implemented
findings.claim: The GNNType enum defines only GAT and MEAN_GNN; a repo-wide grep finds no SGC, GCN, GCNII, or DSS implementation.
findings.concern: Table 5 (MeanGNN / DSS-Mean / TS-Mean, the Q5 'triple-symmetry is necessary' evidence) and Table 6 (TS-SGC / TS-GCN / TS-GCNII) cannot be reproduced because their backbones have no code.
findings.resolution: Provide the SGC/GCN/GCNII aggregations and the DSS-Mean variant, or point to the branch/commit implementing them.

findings.title: No dependency manifest; ogb & scikit-learn undeclared; Neptune logging is mandatory with a placeholder token
findings.quote:
pip3 install torch==2.3.0 torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118
pip3 install torch_scatter torch_sparse torch_cluster torch_spline_conv -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.3.0+cu118.html
pip3 install torch-geometric==2.5.3
pip3 install neptune
pip3 install triton
findings.claim: The only dependency spec is this README block (no requirements.txt / setup.py / environment.yml exists). It omits `ogb` (imported at helpers/datasets.py:16) and `scikit-learn` (imported at transforms/pca.py:3, transforms/least_squares.py:11, helpers/split_data.py:4), and does not pin neptune/triton.
findings.concern: The environment cannot be rebuilt turn-key, and even once built the run cannot start: experiment.py:45 calls `neptune.init_run(project=args.project, api_token=API_TOKEN)` unconditionally with `API_TOKEN = "..."` (constants.py:15) and a required --project, with no offline/disable path.
findings.resolution: Add a pinned requirements file including ogb and scikit-learn; make Neptune logging optional (offline mode / no-op logger) so results can be reproduced without an account.

findings.title: `seed % train_mask.ndim` selects only 2 of the predefined splits, not the seed-th split
findings.quote:
if train_mask.ndim == 2:
    # ! Multiple splits
    # Modified: Use the ${seed} split if not specified!
    split_index = seed
    # Avoid invalid split index
    split_index = (split_index % train_mask.ndim)
    train_mask = train_mask[:, split_index].squeeze()
findings.claim: For datasets with 2-D predefined split masks the split column is `seed % train_mask.ndim`, but `train_mask.ndim` is always 2 for a 2-D tensor, so `split_index = seed % 2 ∈ {0,1}` — contradicting the code's own comment 'Use the ${seed} split'.
findings.concern: Across the 5 seeds (SEEDS=range(5)) only the first two of the many official splits (heterophily/WebKB/Actor ship 10, WikiCS 20) are ever used, and seeds 0/2/4 reuse split 0 while 1/3 reuse split 1, so the reported mean±std over 'five random seeds' does not sample the official splits and understates split variance.
findings.resolution: Use `split_index = seed % train_mask.shape[1]` (or iterate all official splits); re-report Table 1 mean/std with the corrected split selection.

findings.title: Documented 'best config' commands use an undefined --hidden_dim flag and omit --ls_num_layers
findings.claim: The README 'best configs' pass `--hidden_dim 16`, but arguments.py defines `--hid_channel` (there is no `--hidden_dim`); the commands also never pass `--ls_num_layers`, so it stays at the default -1 (LS mixing disabled).
findings.concern: Run verbatim, the documented command aborts with `error: unrecognized arguments: --hidden_dim 16`, and even after renaming the flag it runs the no-least-squares variant rather than the LS-enabled model the paper highlights.
findings.resolution: Fix the README to use `--hid_channel` and add the `--ls_num_layers` value used for the paper's main TS-Mean/TS-GAT results.

findings.title: Paper says per-node L2 normalization; code applies per-feature z-scoring across nodes
findings.claim: `NormalizeTransform` applies `normalize` to `data.x` (normalize.py:24), which subtracts the per-feature mean over nodes (dim=0) and divides by the per-feature std — i.e. column-wise z-scoring across nodes.
findings.concern: The paper states 'we apply L2 normalization to each node's feature vector', which is a per-node (dim=1) unit-norm rescaling; the code implements a different operation (per-feature standardization), a code↔paper mismatch in a core preprocessing step of a feature-invariance method.
findings.resolution: Clarify which normalization was actually used for the reported numbers; if L2-per-node was intended, normalize over dim=1 (row-wise).
findings.paper_ref: §6 Datasets ('L2 normalization to each node's feature vector')

findings.title: co-physics is PCA-reduced to 1024 components in code but 2048 in the paper
findings.claim: The code reduces full_cora and co_cs to 2048 PCA components but co_physics to 1024.
findings.concern: The paper states full-Cora, co-cs, and co-physics are all reduced 'with PCA to 2048 components'; the code uses 1024 for co-physics, a code↔paper discrepancy in the input dimensionality for that dataset.
findings.resolution: Confirm the PCA component count used for co-physics in the reported runs and reconcile paper text with code.

findings.title: Paper says Adam; code uses AdamW (decoupled weight decay)
findings.claim: Training uses `torch.optim.AdamW` (which applies decoupled weight decay, default 0.01).
findings.concern: The paper states 'We optimize all models using the Adam optimizer'; AdamW is a different optimizer (nonzero default weight decay), a code↔paper mismatch that can shift the reported results.
findings.resolution: State whether AdamW (and what weight decay) or plain Adam was used for the reported numbers.
findings.paper_ref: §6 ('We optimize all models using the Adam optimizer')

findings.title: align_masks unions train+test, so evaluated nodes' labels are fed to the model at test time
findings.quote:
train_mask = data.train_mask
test_mask = data.test_mask
if train_mask.ndim > test_mask.ndim:
    test_mask = test_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(train_mask)
elif test_mask.ndim > train_mask.ndim:
    train_mask = train_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(test_mask)
data.train_mask = train_mask | test_mask
return data
findings.claim: For every dataset with predefined splits, `align_masks` sets `train_mask = train_mask | test_mask` (leaving `test_mask` unchanged), so `test_mask ⊆ train_mask`. Downstream, `train_mask` is the model's visible label/support set: the least-squares mixers are fit on `data.*[data.train_mask]` (least_squares.py:108,112,122-132), and at eval `train_y[~data.train_mask]=0` (experiment.py:243-244) with `lp_mask = train_mask` (gfm.py:74,80) feeds those labels through the layers (each backbone has a self/root term); the same nodes are then scored via `test_mask` (experiment.py:249).
findings.concern: The labels of the evaluated (test) nodes are visible to the model — both as least-squares targets and as propagated labels — while those nodes are scored, so the reported 'zero-shot test accuracy' on the ~15 predefined-split datasets (citeseer, pubmed, roman-empire, amazon-ratings, minesweeper, tolokers, questions, chameleon, squirrel, cornell, wisconsin, texas, actor, wiki-cs, arxiv) is not a clean held-out estimate; the ~13 datasets that instead use `graphany_mask_splits` (disjoint 20·C train nodes) are unaffected.
findings.resolution: Re-run with the evaluated test nodes excluded from `data.train_mask` (both the LS fit and the label-propagation support), and report the change in Table 1/Figure 3; confirm whether `align_masks`' union is intended and matches the GraphAny protocol it cites.
